introduction: This fourth Sunday of Easter is Good Shepherd Sunday, and the Church prays today for vocations. Jesus tells us that he is the good shepherd who lays down his life for his sheep, knows them, and goes after the sheep not yet in his fold. Peter proclaims that there is salvation in no other name. John marvels that we are called children of God. Let us listen to the voice of our shepherd and follow him.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the good shepherd knows each of us by name. Let us bring our prayers to the Father with confidence.
intentions: For our Pope, our bishop and all the shepherds of the Church: that they may care for God's people with the heart of the good shepherd. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood, the diaconate and religious life: that young people may hear Christ's call and answer it with joy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel lost or far from the flock: that the good shepherd may find them and bring them home. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christian unity: that there may be one flock with one shepherd. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves and our families: that we may know the voice of Jesus and follow him every day. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, good shepherd, you laid down your life for your sheep. Raise up shepherds after your own heart, and gather all people into your one flock. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: The good shepherd
reflection.body:
In the time of Jesus, a shepherd lived with his sheep day and night. He knew each one, and they knew his voice. When Jesus says, "I am the good shepherd," he is speaking about a relationship, not a job.

He sets the good shepherd beside the hired hand. When the wolf comes, the hired hand runs away, because he "doesn't care for the sheep." The good shepherd stays, even at the cost of his life: "The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." And he does it freely. "No one takes it away from me, but I lay it down by myself." On the cross, that is exactly what happened.

Jesus also looks beyond the people in front of him: "I have other sheep which are not of this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice." His heart is as wide as the world. "They will become one flock with one shepherd."

In the first reading, Peter is on trial for healing a crippled man. He uses the occasion to proclaim Jesus: "There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved!" And John invites us to wonder at what this shepherd has made us: "See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!"

Today the Church prays for vocations. Christ still calls men and women to serve as shepherds and to give their lives to him. Pray for them by name: the priests who baptized you, heard your confession or buried your loved ones. If you know a young person who might be called, encourage them. And listen for the shepherd's voice in your own life this week: in the Scriptures, in prayer and in the people who guide you.
